column1: # One row per narration segment, in order. Tab-separated. '#' comments and blank lines ignored.
# seg   clip    in      speed   crop    chip
# in    seconds to seek into the clip before the segment starts (skips page load / layout shift)
# speed playback multiplier. Mostly slightly BELOW 1 here: agent-browser only emits a frame when
#       pixels change, so a clip of a mostly-still page is shorter than its wall time and has to be
#       stretched to cover its narration.
# crop  W:H:X:Y in MASTER coordinates (3200x1800), or '-' for the full frame. Crops are what make
#       the narrated text legible — a crop is a real zoom into the 2x master, not an upscale.
# chip  burnt-in label, or '-'. Declared per shot rather than derived from `speed`, because the
#       capture itself already compresses idle time: clip_run is 166s of video for a 315s run, so
#       the elapsed counter visibly runs ~2x even at speed=1, and that has to be labelled. A
#       slow-motion shot (speed<1) must never be labelled as sped up.
# seg05/seg06 are two windows into one continuous recording of the live run.
# seg07/seg08 come from a deliberate replay pass over the finished run: the event timeline never
# auto-scrolls, so the live take sits still on the left for minutes — the exact dead air that got
# v1 rejected. The run is a permanent replayable record, so it is driven on purpose instead.
